utterances.text: So the Bosnian Serbs decided to hold a referendum among its citizens on the question of the Vance-Owen Plan. What was the FRY leadership's response to this position that RS, the Republika Srpska, adopted?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have Rule 65 ter number 02306.01 on the screen, please. And I need the second document which is attached to that Rule 65 ter number in e-court, and so it's not the -- I'm advised that it's not the document marked with the ERN number with "-EDT" at the end of it. It's the other one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, this is the transcript of the 30th Bosnian Serb assembly session held Jahorina on the 5th and 6th of May 1993.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. It's the 30th session, and not the 39th session as described in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who was in attendance at this meeting from the FRY leadership?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Present at this meeting were the same people that signed the letter that reference has been made to, that is Dobrica Cosic, Slobodan Milosevic, and Momir Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did all three of these gentlemen speak at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What did Dobrica Cosic say?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He gave a short speech.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So first of all what -- what -- why did the Serb leadership attend this Bosnian Serb Assembly session?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their purpose was the same as the letter which was to encourage the Bosnian Serbs to accept the plan which Radovan Karadzic had provisionally done a few days before at a meeting in Athens, but only provisionally.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have page 26 of the English translation and page 12 of the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What did -- what did Dobrica Cosic have to say at this Assembly session?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he encouraged acceptance of the plan, and he noted the -- that at this point the Serbs were at a turning point in their history. If I could direct the Court's attention to the fourth paragraphs -- fourth paragraph of his speech beginning with. "We are truly at a turning point in our history. That historic turning point has often been like a temptation in our past. We have shared a common goal for two centuries, the struggle for liberation and the union of the Serbian people. This is the seventh war to be waged with this goal."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what did Slobodan Milosevic put forth at this meeting? And if we could go to page 163 of the English translation and 78 of the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He also encouraged the Assembly to accept the plan and also addressed the issue of the unity of the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could just pause there. If Your Honours wish to see where Slobodan Milosevic begins his speech, it's at page 157 of the English translation and page 76 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Treanor. Can you continue.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would draw the Court's attention in that connection to two passages on page 163 of the English translation. The first passage begins on the line starting with question mark use, and the first sentence reads: "Above all the question now arises as to how we shall link the economies of the provinces that are ours. Since you are deputies you probably know that we have established a single-payment transfer system, that we are moving towards a single currency, that we are moving towards every possible link and transaction between the economies, that we are moving towards a stabilised, a whole single economic areas where the Serbian lands here will be from the aspect of the economy and culture and education and everything else. Karadzic spoke of the same primer, et cetera. Therefore, not a lot of thought is required in order to envisage the direction that this process -- that process needs to go in."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned two paragraphs. What was the second section on that page?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a little bit below he continues: "Finally I should like to say to you don't talk to us who have been worrying about all your problems all this time, about feeling abandoned. We didn't just sit -- sit about worrying about them but resolved them and helped with all our might and with everything that we could at the cost of great deprivation to a Serbia of 10 million, and we shall continue to help you. There's no question about that. But don't tell us that you feel abandoned, because that is incorrect."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may those documents -- those pages be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They are so --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's page -- sorry, page 126 and 163 of the English translation and pages 112 and 78 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess you also referred the Chamber to page 157 for the Milosevic's speech. Don't you want that in?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's -- Your Honour, that's where -- the page where Slobodan Milosevic's name is first mentioned, but we don't seek to have that page into evidence. It was simply if you wanted to see on the screen where his name was first mentioned as he began the speech.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Sutherland. Those pages are therefore admitted into evidence. May they please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P211, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, we will have a revised page 1 of the English translation where it says the 39th session will be amended to the 30th session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But -- yeah, thank you so much for doing that, but what is the status of that translation? Is it --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's a draft translation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's a draft translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: By CLSS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: By CLSS. Thank you. Could you ask them to revise it, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, what did the Bosnian Serbs do as a result of the FRY leadership's pleas?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they maintained their position and -- they being the Assembly maintained its position and went ahead with the plebiscite that it -- they'd already called for and scheduled it for the middle of May, and it was, in fact, held and rejected the plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did the Security Council take any measures in relation to the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina after the expiration of the deadline they had imposed in the earlier Resolution?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter number 06622 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What measures did the Security Council take and when?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the 6th of May, 1993, it adopted Resolution 824 in which it extended the --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- idea of safe areas to cities and towns in BH beyond Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we go to page 2 of the English translation and page 3 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would call the Court's attention to paragraph 3 in that connection, which I will refrain from reading, but it does make reference to the -- the capital of BH and other threatened areas, in particular, the towns of Tuzla, Zepa, Bihac, as well as Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The capital of BH being Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They should all be treated as safe areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And did it make any declarations in relation to these safe areas? I mean further declarations?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in paragraph 4 it declared what should be observed in the safe areas, for instance, A, the immediate cessation of armed attacks or any hostile act against these safe areas and the withdrawal of all Bosnian Serb military or paramilitary units from these towns to a distance wherefrom they cease to constitute a menace to their security and that of their inhabitance to be monitored by United Nations military observers, and it goes on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may that document be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P212, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, you discussed earlier in your evidence a meeting, a Bosnian Serb Assembly session that was held on the 5th and 6th of May 1993 in Jahorina. Did Slobodan Milosevic, who was in attendance at that meeting, did he report back to the FRY leadership about the meeting that was held in Jahorina on the 5th and 6th of May?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have Rule 65 ter number 06980.01. This is the redacted version of that exhibit. And if we could have page 29 of the B/C/S and page 31 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document represents shorthand notes of a session of the Supreme Defence Council of the FRY held on the 2nd of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what did Slobodan Milosevic say in relation to the discussions that he'd had with the Serbs at the Assembly session?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told the people present at the meeting certain things that he had told the Bosnian Serb leaders, and in that connection I would draw the Court's attention to page 31 of the translation, which is page 29 in the original.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, are you able to tell the Court what Milosevic said?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we go to the top of the page in -- in the English translation, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, reading from -- Mr. Treanor, you can see the redacted text on the screen.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, beginning with "I used to tell them," that is the Bosnian Serb leaders, "if our economy fails, who will you rely on? They could have resolved the problem by means of the solution that has been offered. They could have accepted it," that is the peace plan, "which would have annulled the second round of sanctions. The sanctions would have failed they would not have been implemented while the Muslim-Croat conflict in Central Bosnia would have ruined the plan. Any literate man can see it."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what, in your view, did Slobodan Milosevic -- what was the reference to, "If we economically collapse, who will you lean on?" What do you understand that to mean?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's referring to the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: "If we," being the FRY, "economically collapse."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "If our economy fails, the FRY, who will you, the Bosnian Serbs, rely on?"

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I take you now to a few months after that date.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, can that page be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The page is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Page 1 and page 31 of the English translation and page 1 and page 29 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Those pages.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Those pages will be Exhibit P213, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, do you infer from this comment, "if we economically collapse, who will you lean on," that the Bosnian Serbs had been up until that point relying on the FRY lead -- the FRY?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The document speaks for itself. The statement speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I withdraw my question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, did the FRY continue to support the RS military, the Republika Srpska military? If I could have 65 ter number [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- 02144.01 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you say that again please, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the record that's already admitted as Exhibit P200.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Oh, thank you. Except that only certain pages were admitted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- when the document was last used, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, as I see it, Exhibit 200 doesn't have the .01. It's just 02144, page 354.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it does have .01 at the end of it. P200. The Rule 65 ter number is the same as this one. Back when we discussed it before, only page 354 was admitted into evidence, the statement by General Gvero, the one page of his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I withdraw my last question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, in relation to this document, as you know it's the transcript of the continuation of the 34th session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly held in Jahorina over quite a number of dates. Did Radovan Karadzic make any reference to the strategic goals in this Assembly session?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we go to page 14 to 15 of the English translation and pages 13 to 14 of the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What did Dr. Karadzic say in that regard?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that regard I would draw the Court's attention to the paragraph toward the bottom of the page beginning with "Strategic goals." That paragraph reads: "Strategic goals adopted by this Assembly have been or will be achieved to the fullest extent, just to remind those who do not know it. This Assembly reached strategic goals of Serb people, which have become, in a certain way, our tasks, our obligation to realise them, but those were the goals we aimed at and the goals we aim at now to achieve whenever it would be possible." Then he goes on as, I would call the Court's attention, to describe each of the goals. Going over to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this is in August 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This speech was actually given on the first day of the session, on the 27th of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may those pages be admitted into evidence as part as P200.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They are so admitted. May they please be given an exhibit number. Oh, as part of 200? Okay they will go in as part of 200.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, in your review of documentation, have you viewed any correspondence between the Bosnian Serb political leadership and General Momcilo Perisic?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter number 00599 on the screen, please. It's a one-page document in B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What is this document and when is it dated?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is a letter from Momcilo Krajisnik, who is the president of the Bosnian Serb Assembly, to General Momcilo Perisic, dated 27 September 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what is -- what is the substance of the letter?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the letter refers to a meeting in Belgrade and a telephone conversation, a conversation -- the telephone conversation also took place on the 27th of September, and it goes on to refer to assistance. "The assistance would be sent to the Sarajevo area, because in the coming two-year period the battle for our part of Sarajevo is impending." Then he goes on to thank General Perisic. "General Perisic, you have done a lot for these people. We are now in such a situation that we have to ask for help, but the time will come when we will be able to repay the debt."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may that document admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The exhibit is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P214, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, did the FRY continue to provide military assistance to the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Have you seen any new documents that reflect the ultimate goal of the FRY leadership?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did General Perisic have knowledge of this goal?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would ask to go into closed session to deal with a document that's the subject of protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you want closed session or private session?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It needs to be closed session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session. 25 [Closed session] [Confidentiality lifted by later order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, what was the goal of the FRY leadership?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter number 09190.01 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That goal is stated a number of times in the document we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: First, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is a directive for the use of the Yugoslav army, RS army in the Serb Armija -- army of Krajina. It was issued by president Zoran Lilic on 14 November 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In what capacity did Zoran Lilic issue this decision -- this directive?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As president of the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you please continue. I -- I interrupted you to get the -- the date of the document and the name of the document.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The goal is referred to a number of times in this document. In that connection I would call the Court's attention to the first paragraph of the body of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what is the goal?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Toward the end of that paragraph reference is made to "...two new Serbian states which are determined to fight the war imposed on them in order to defend their republics and establish conditions for the creation of a single state of the Serbian people."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You said that this goal was referred to a number of times in this document.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In that connection I could call the Court's attention --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Go to page 7 of the English translation and page 7 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under Roman II, use of armed forces, 1, General objectives. The second paragraph states: "Defend territorial integrity of the Serbian States west of the Drina and Danube rivers and FRY, protect Serbian people from genocide, liberate parts of Serbian territories with Serbian majority, create conditions for the establishment of a single state of the Serbian people, prevent creation of Greater Croatia and a compact Islamic state on the territory of the former Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could take you to page 9 of the English translation and page 8 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would call the Court's attention to the middle of the page, the paragraph beginning "In the second," which word is bolded. The second referring to the second stage of operations. "In the second, after the beginning of the all-out HV aggression on the RSK and armed rebellion in crisis regions of the FRY, by the unified use of armed forces of the Serbian people crush and defeat enemy forces and create conditions for establishing a single state of the Serbian people."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then if we could go to page 12 of the English translation and also page 12 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very bottom of the page under IV, combat operations support, 1, moral guidance and psychological support. "Ensure that all activities on boosting, maintaining, and reinforcing combat morale of the army proceed from the firm determination of the state and political leadership of the Serbian people to protect the people, defend territory and create conditions for the formation of a single state of the Serbian people. Pursuant to this, intensify information and propaganda activities and build united public support."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this document be admitted into evidence. It's -- it's quite lengthy, so I would ask that the pages that I have taken Mr. Treanor to be admitted, and that is -- well, perhaps so that Your Honours can put it into context, the first 12 pages of the document in English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But why the first 12 pages? I understand context where I -- why do we need so many pages for context?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Well, you don't, Your Honour. It's just that I took Mr. Treanor to pages 1, 2, 7, 9 and 12. 1, 2, 7, 9, and 12, so I took him to 5 of the first 12 pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document -- those pages are admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, since the document was used in closed session, should it be --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P215 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honours, is that just the pages I took Mr. Treanor to, or is it the first 12 pages of the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The first 12 pages.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, we can go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, did the Republika Srpska or the Bosnian Serb leadership continue to be satisfied with what they had achieved on the territory?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Why was this?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not satisfied. The Bosnian Serb was not satisfied, which is why they'd rejected the Vance Plan. Negotiations did continue. A plan had been formulated in the fall of 1993, known as the Owen-Stoltenberg Plan. That was signed by the Bosnian Serbs and the Bosnian Croats but not by the Bosnian Muslims, and subsequent to that, negotiations continued.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have Rule 65 ter number 02336 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a transcript of the 37th session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly held in Pale on the 10th of January, 1994. At this session does Radovan Karadzic make explicit reference to the strategic goals?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could take you to page 108 of the English translation and page 80 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would call the Court's attention to a short passage in the middle -- toward the beginning -- toward the top of that page. The line begins with "Themselves as Yugoslavs," and then continues: "Believe me we are the winners so far compared to what we could have got from it. We could have got the separation. The first strategic goal was separation, not occupation of 60 per cent of it. The second strategic goal was to get the land in one piece interconnected, and we got the corridor. So that was the strategic goal. As the opposing faction, we won our state and that was accepted. And secondly, as winners we said, 'Fine. You want 33.3 per cent, we will determine which 33.3 per cent you can get.'"

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What was Radovan Karadzic referring to when he said that? He was referring to the state of the negotiations at that particular time, emphasising what they could achieve at that particular time. Unfortunately, the negotiations did not result in -- in any agreement at this time or indeed for months and months to come.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may that page be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's so admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P216, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, pages 1 and 108 of the English translation and pages 1 and 80 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I want to move on four months into April 1994. At this time did the Belgrade leadership want to -- to freeze the combat activity in Bosnia-Herzegovina and, if so, why?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The FRY leadership?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The FRY leadership continued to favour the conclusion of peace.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for much the same reasons that had been adduced before, that is, they thought the important thing was to get what had been achieved recognised by the international community, and they were also suffering under the sanctions at this time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter number 06639.01, which is the redacted version of this document, on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, we can see that this is the stenographic notes of the 20th session of the SDC. What was discussed at this session in relation to Bosnia and Herzegovina in relation to what you have just discussed?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certainly the points that I just mentioned were discussed at this session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could -- if we could go to page 6 of the English translation and page 4 of the B/C/S. Mr. Treanor, did General Perisic have anything to say at this meeting --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- about what you've just discussed?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He -- he addressed one of the points I mentioned, noting that at the bottom of the page, the paragraph beginning with "Fourth." "Fourth, our chances to control the crisis are based on the following: that we continue disrupting their scenario," that is the enemy's scenario, "as we have done so far. We have almost completely realised our objectives with weapons. We must maintain this and with wise politics before the international community manage somehow to have it all endorsed."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And Slobodan Milosevic make any -- have any discussion on these points?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to page 7 of the English translation and page 8 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those pages do not correspond.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm sorry. Before we go to Mr. Milosevic, there's another -- there's another portion of these -- this session that I'd like to take you to where Mr. Perisic is speaking, and it's on page 7 of the English translation and page 5 of the B/C/S. Mr. Treanor, what does Mr. Perisic say in relation to the -- the issue of Gorazde?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just below --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, if I could take you to the -- the paragraph starting "The measures which in our opinion ought to be undertaken."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At this portion he's recommending certain measures, and reference to Gorazde is made among them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What are the measures that he is discussing?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the paragraph beginning with "The measures, which in our opinion, ought to be taken," he mentions developing a broad diplomatic activity with all participants of the Yugoslav crisis, with the objective of crowning the war results and verifying them by international recognition. In the second paragraph he recommends approaching countries and individuals who favour us, saying "we should encourage import of weapons and military equipment which in event of the escalation of the conflict, we would use for inflicting the greatest possible losses on the enemy, especially hitting air targets because anti-aircraft defence is far weaker than it should be." And the next brief paragraph he addresses Gorazde mentioning that the bombing of positions in the Gorazde sector ought to be used for strengthening the unity of all forces defending the national interest --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel slow down, please. -- reading for the interpreters, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The bombing of positions in the Gorazde sector ought to be used for strengthening the unity of all forces defending the national interest of the Serbian and Montenegrin peoples.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that a convenient point, madam? SUTHERLAND: Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We will take a break and come back at 12.30. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, before the break we were discussing the stenographic notes of the 20th session of the SDC.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we have page 7 of the English translation and page 8 of the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What did Slobodan Milosevic say at this meeting in regard to the points that you were discussing before the break?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he advanced the idea that he thought it would be a good idea to freeze military operations in Bosnia-Herzegovina at this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can I take you to the paragraph beginning "Our first-rate goal at the moment --" starting "As for this situation..."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Registry have informed me that we're actually on page 12 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What does he say in relation to the territory that the forces control at the moment or back in April 1994?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this paragraph he notes that at this point they were in a situation when "...our forces control 72 per cent of the territory," and he thought that would create a very good position for finalising negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Does he make any mention in this session to the Drina -- to the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he does. A little bit further below in that same paragraph he makes reference to the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And briefly, what does say about that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He says: "I believe that we are moving toward a solution in general cease of hostilities on the establishment of the front demarcation of the -- of the front demarcation line, including the right Drina bank near Gorazde because it would not be in our interest to abandon the right bank of the Drina."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And does he say what the political solution has to be based on?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He sees as part of the overall solution at this point the lifting of sanctions against the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may those pages that I've taken Mr. Treanor to be admitted into evidence. That is pages 1, 2, 6, and 12 of the English translation and 1, 4, 5, 8, and 9 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Those pages are admitted into evidence. May they please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, 12 and 13 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Those pages will be Exhibit P217, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned a moment ago that it was Slobodan Milosevic's position that they -- that the Bosnian Serbs should freeze the combat activity. What was -- what was the Bosnian Serbs' position in respect of that? Did they agree?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 02150.01 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at this point at which -- during which negotiations were still proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I can take you to the document that's on the screen now. It's the minutes of the 40th session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly held in Brcko on the 10th of May, 1994. Did Radovan Karadzic make reference to the strategic goals during this session?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we have page 41 of the English translation and page 37 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I seem to have directed you to the wrong page.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's 36 in the English -- I'm sorry, 41, which is 36 in the original.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what Karadzic said at that session in relation to the strategic goals?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I direct the Court's attention to the first full paragraph in the English translation, and the line beginning with "percentage." He says: "We have to get out to get the state which we would verify. We have to end this war as soon as possible, and believe me, we often have the difficult discussion and conversations with our army. There is no pay that we can take the whole Bosnia. I don't want to tell you what the economy we need for such project. It is not the strategic goal of this Assembly. The goal is to separate ourselves. We did not say, then, how much a percentage, nor did we outline the borders. But we said we wanted to separate, and strategic goals would be territorial connection with the Drina River, Neretva River, sea, Sarajevo, Sava River, Una River, et cetera."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And at that stage of proceedings in May 1994, what -- where were the negotiations at?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were more or less at a standstill at this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And why was that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the previous plans had been adopted, had been accepted now by one side, now another, and another agreement accepted by different side but rejected by another. So everyone had stated their positions at this point and were sticking to them. At this point in the spring of 1994, the so-called Contact Group was formed to try to get the process going again. The Contact Group was a group of states including Russia, the United States, and some of the EU countries to try to break the logjam, if you will, that had occurred in the ICFY process, that is the process that was under the auspices of the Conference on the Former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What was the percentage of the territory that the Bosnian Serbs were being offered at this time?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Contact Group was about to offer them a map that would give them 49 per cent of the territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you had made mention earlier that they had achieved through their combat forces 70 per cent of the territory; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. I think that we just saw someone saying even 72 per cent by the spring of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the pages that I've taken Mr. Treanor be admitted into evidence? That's page 1 and 41 of the English translation and page 1 and 37 of the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They are so admitted. May they please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 212 -- 218, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now I'd like to take you to the middle of the year 1994. Did the Bosnian Serb leadership have further discussions with the FRY leadership re: The Contact Group plan?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have Rule 65 ter number 02151.01.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, this is a document -- a transcript of the 42nd Bosnian Serb Assembly session held in Pale on the 18th and 19th of July, 1994. Who was in attendance at this Assembly session from the FRY leadership?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think anyone from the leadership was there, the FRY leadership.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In relation to the further discussions that the FRY leadership had with the Bosnian Serbs about the Contact Group plan, when did that occur?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There had been a meeting early in the morning of the 18th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you -- are you aware of what was discussed at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, are we referring to a meeting wherein there was a document? A document -- that meeting was documented or was this a chitchat over coffee? I'm not sure exactly where we are.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The document that's on the screen is the transcript of the 42nd Bosnian Serb Assembly session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's correct, but the witness then said there had been a meeting also early that morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just about to ask a follow-up question, Your Honour, in relation to how he knows of that meeting. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, you may, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, how do you know there was a meeting at 4.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Momcilo Krajisnik refers to that meeting during this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have page 28 of the English translation and page 115 of the B/C/S on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What does Momcilo Krajisnik say at the Assembly in relation to the meeting that was had at 4.00 a.m. in the morning?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two paragraphs on the page we're looking at that relate to that meeting. At the top of the page Mr. Krajisnik said: "We'd had discussions with representatives of Serbia and Montenegro until 4.00 this morning. This is not a secret at all. They think that we have to accept it. We said, we do not have to. We cannot accept it. We led the way for our people, and we will lead them as long as we could. When we cannot, then Kecmanovic will come in," he is another Serbian politician, "and let him take the lead and sign it then, if the people accept it. General Perisic was there, as well as our General Mladic, Tolimir. Everyone in our delegation said that we did not accept it. None of us said that this could be. But you should understand that we have to find a way - it is not enough that we just say no, and we do not care about it anymore. There is no we do not care. We have to win. We want a state. We do not want half the Serbs dead. I am not afraid of their bombing. They will not bomb. We have to find a way, have to continue the negotiations." And below he says a little bit more about the meeting, in relation to the meeting, two paragraphs below that beginning with: "Chairman, I will try to be as much open as I can, though it is not correct that I am this much open. We have problems in getting supplies from Serbia because of poor resources. I will not say whether this is on purpose or not. I know that all the resources are used up, and we can by no means not to talk with Serbia, nor would it be good. We went to talk. It is true that Serbia and Montenegro, Mr. Bulatovic and Mr. Milosevic were there. They presented a complete picture. We said that everything was like that, the partisans and people who fought between '41 and '45, they fought without a single bullet and without weapons. We will fight against the Muslims, and we'll snatch their weapons. We cannot accept this because this is a unitary Bosnia. Our standpoint was clear."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may that page of that document be admitted into evidence, please. That is page 1 and page 28 of the English translation and page 1 and page 115 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Those pages are admitted into evidence. May they please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P219, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Shortly after that meeting did the Bosnian Serb leadership issue a declaration of their objectives regarding the Contact Group plan negotiations?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 02153 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: When did they do this?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the original declaration was adopted at the 42nd session that we just considered, and they expanded on that declaration, adopting what they call explanations that were to be part of the declaration at the next session, the 43rd session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to page 5 of the English translation and page 6 of the B/C/S, please. And were the -- the explanations read into the record.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And can you please summarise the statement of reasons for the Court. What were they saying in their -- the statement of reasons that was to be attached to the declaration?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Very briefly, they -- the Bosnian Serb Assembly offered to continue negotiations on the basis of the Contact Group plan, and under point 2 I would point out that they state: "In the belief that the international community will ensure that the following shall be achieved through these negotiations: A, further adjustments to the map; B, demarcation in the city of Sarajevo and the province of Sarajevo; C, a solution for access to the sea for Republika Srpska; D, the exercise of the right of peoples to self-determination, including the right of linking up as a state with neighbouring states; and, E, an agreement on the cessation of hostilities, implementation of the plan, and lifting sanctions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may those pages be admitted into evidence. That is pages 1 and 5 of the English translation and pages 1 and 6 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They are so admitted. They may be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: They will be Exhibit P220, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Following this statement of reasons and the declaration, did the FRY leadership assert any pressure on the Bosnian Serb leadership to accept the Contact Group plan?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What kind of pressure?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have Rule 65 ter number 06828 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of August, Slobodan Milosevic issued a public statement in connection with that matter, and the FRY government made a decision, which was also made public.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What was the public statement that Milosevic issued?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a statement published in the Belgrade press on the 5th of August, he said, among other things, that they, the Bosnian Serbs --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if we could go to page 4 and 5 of the English translation. It's on page 1 of the B/C/S. It's the article on the right-hand side of the page, top right-hand side of the page. Go on, Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the paragraph toward the middle of the page beginning with "They reject a peace," he said: "They reject a peace in a moment when they have a recognised Republika Srpska which encompasses half of the territory of the former Bosnia and Herzegovina, and by accepting peace sanctions would be lifted for those without whom they would not even exist." And he goes on to say something about the measures they're going to take in view of the situation, which is on the next page, toward the very end of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, if pages 4 and 5 of that document could be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They are so admitted. May they please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: They will be Exhibit P221, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What are the measures that are going to be taken in -- in view of the situation?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I mentioned, the federal government adopted a decision on the 4th of August, which was published in the press on the 5th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And, if I understood you, then the measures were going to be that they were going to sever relations; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Was that -- what was their position?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the -- a statement was issued at --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if I could -- if we could -- no, sorry. I apologise, Your Honour. Could I have 65 ter number 09175 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What measures did the FRY leadership take in relation to the Republika Srpska at this time?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the press report that I referred to on the 5th of August, in the middle of the page in English or -- it says "Belgrade." We can see that the report says: "The federal government took the decision in a meeting yesterday to cut all political and economic ties with Republika Srpska." And then it goes on to quote a statement that was issued after the meeting to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may that document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P222, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did this, in fact, occur, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were certain measures that were taken, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Were relations cut off economically and politically?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think we'll be seeing documents shortly that would indicate that that was not the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The answer is that they didn't. They didn't cut --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- economic and political relations.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That would be the short answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's try and be short, and concise and to the point. Yes, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, notwithstanding this apparent rupture in relations, did Republika Srpska leadership still want one state?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the other Serbs, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 06735 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did they issue any proposals in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 18th of August, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What was the proposal?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: A -- it was a proposition for the integration of the Republic of Serbia, the Republic of Montenegro, the Serbian republic in the Serbian Krajina, into one state adopted by the Assemblies of the Republika Srpska. I think we're seeing this translated as "Republic of Serbia," but it's Republika Srpska, and the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure I understand that answer. You say that the transcript says it was a proposition for the integration of the Republic of Serbia, the Republic of Montenegro, the Serbian republic in the Serbian Krajina into one state, adopted by the assemblies of the Republika Srpska. What does that mean, that last phrase, adopted by the Assemblies of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Assemblies of the Republika Srpska and of the Republic of Serbia and Krajina, both adopted that proposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But that is what that sentence is saying?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think the second -- I thought I said after Republika Srpska, the Republic of Serbian Krajina. I also noted that here Republika Srpska is translated as Republic of Serbia, and it's translated further on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you give the correct answer to that question now, just afresh?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The proposition for the integration of the Republic of Serbia, the Republic of Montenegro, Republika Srpska, and the Republic of the Serbian Krajina into one state was adopted by the Assemblies of Republika Srpska and of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, if I may just ask, are you able to tell us from where the proposition came or from whom it came?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's based on the right to national self-determination, et cetera. It says that the Assembly of Republika Srpska and the Assembly of Republic of Serbian Krajina decided to. So it came from them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So it was not a proposition made to them. It was a decision by them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They're making the proposition in effect to -- if I could direct your attention to paragraph number 1 under the title of the proposition, being the next page in English. Next page in English, please. Where it states: "We ask the Assembly," "we" being the Assemblies of Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina, "We ask the Assembly of the Republic of Serbia and the Republic of Montenegro to accept the proposition for the integration into one state ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. So they are propositioning. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note this is a final translation from CLSS, but given the differences in translation, I would ask that we ask CLSS to review this translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But I thought Mr. Treanor has now given us testimony that is in line with the translation. He has corrected what was said there earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, if -- if I may, at the top of page 1 of the -- of the English translation, it says the Republic of Serbia National Assembly on the first page, on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And if we can have a look at the first page, please. Republic of Serbia -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And Mr. Treanor's saying that that should be Republika Srpska National Assembly, and then on the right-hand side you have the Republic of Serbian Krajina Assembly, and then it's going to the National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia and the National Assembly of the Republic of Montenegro, the proposition. And then on page 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure, I -- do you endorse that, Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It should be the republic of --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Republika Srpska. Any comment to make, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yeah, we will do so, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May that be marked -- admitted into evidence and marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. It is so admitted. May it be so marked and given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P223, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor had the Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina taken -- previously taken steps to unite?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as between themselves. Between those two entities they had adopted a declaration, a joint session of their Assemblies in, I believe, November 1992 in Prijedor about the unification of their two legal systems and beginning a process of discussion of uniting those two entities, which was developed over the next several months in meetings between a commission that was set up.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. Now, taking you back to August 1994, which is the document that we have just discussed. Was the FRY leadership satisfied at this point with the Contact Group plan? If I could have Rule 65 ter number 06640.01, which is the redacted version of that exhibit on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The FRY leadership continued to favour acceptance of the plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: At this -- the document that's on the screen before us is the stenographic notes of the 25th session of the SDC session. Did Slobodan Milosevic -- or what did Slobodan Milosevic say in this session in relation to the -- to the Contact Group plan?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He made some statements in support of accepting the plan and critical of the Bosnian Serb leadership --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And if --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- for not doing so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- we could go to page 37 of the English translation, and page 24 of the B/C/S. What is Mr. Milosevic's position?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, in the paragraph -- first paragraph in the English translation, he says that "by pursuing a unanimous policy and quite successfully in my mind, we have managed to save the country from war, and at the same rendered as much support as possible to our people across the Drina and creating the Republika Srpska and creating the Republic of Srpska Krajina and in winning them a normal status by the negotiations, leading to an ultimate goal, which now even the international community has offered to recognise. And that is Republika Srpska stretching over half of the territory of the former Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I take you, please, to page 2 -- sorry, page 25 of the B/C/S -- 27 of the B/C/S and page 41 of the English translation. Does he talk there about the territory, the amount of territory that the Bosnian Serbs have? I'm sorry, no. Not in relation to the Bosnian Serbs but in relation to Serb territory.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's referring to the territory that has been offered. He says: "We have actually been offered to expand the territory by one-fourth, because Yugoslavia's territory is 102.000 square kilometres and to increase the population by one-tenth and to legalise it as well and even to have a confederation right away. Koziryev told me that quite clearly. The leadership of Republika Srpska knows that, in that way, we shall be given the right to legally defend those borders. This rules the Iraqi syndrome of illegally entering a territory and then being exposed to strikes," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can I take you to page 28 of the B/C/S and page 42 of the English translation. Does Slobodan Milosevic make reference to goals being fulfilled?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He refers on this page in the paragraph beginning "we were in a situation to the establishment of a -- of Republika Srpska." And he says: "We were in a situation which obviously leads down this dangerous path. Seeing how things are going with Republika Srpska, it is possible that the achievement represented by the offer from the international community for Republika Srpska to be constituted on one-half of the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina and immediately form a confederation with Yugoslavia will simply be annihilated. This will lay the groundwork for the Serbs to practically remain living in one state, and incomparably increase the chances for a favourable future solution for the Republic of Serbian Krajina, whereby all our goals would have been achieved."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may pages 1, 37, 41, and 42 of the English translation and pages 1, 24, 27, and 28 be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They are so admitted. May they please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P224, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, what was the Security Council's reaction to the Republika Srpska's refusal to accept the Contact Group plan?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it passed a Resolution endorsing that plan, and --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 02179 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On putting further restrictions on commercial and other activities with the territory of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What was the Security Council's -- in this Resolution, what were they -- what were they trying to prevent?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we can see that in the second page of the English, they give a very brief statement under B.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If you can actually summarise that for the Chamber, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly won't to read the whole thing, but the first paragraph states that the Security Council resolved to reinforce --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please read slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Security Council resolved to reinforce and extend the measures imposed by its previous Resolutions with regard to those areas of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina under the control of Bosnian Serb forces - and then just I call attention the Chamber to numbered paragraph 6 - it called upon states to desist from any political talks with the leadership of the Bosnian Serb party as long as that party has not accepted the proposed settlement in full.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could take you to paragraph 14 on page -- pages 4 and 5 of the English translation and page 4 and 5 of the B/C/S. What basically is paragraph 14 requiring parties to do or states to do?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's requiring them to prevent the entry into their territory of certain officials of the Bosnian Serb republic, including legislative authorities and officers of the Bosnian Serb military and paramilitary forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may that Security Council Resolution be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P225, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did the FRY leadership maintain its support for the Contact Group plan?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just the UN Resolution that we just looked at, P225, what was the date of that Resolution?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: UN Security Council Resolution 942 was adopted on the 23rd of September, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Going forward to November 1994, you said that the FRY leadership did maintain support for the Contact Group plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 06677 on the screen, please -- 06677.01, the redacted version of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor this is the stenographic notes of the 28th session of the SDC held on the 2nd of November, 1994. What did Slobodan Milosevic express at this SDC meeting in relation to its support for the Bosnian Serbs in Republika Srpska? And if I could take you to paragraph -- sorry, page 30 of the English translation and page 29 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I apologise. Perhaps I'm a bit confused. There was a question pending, and I thought that this particular document dealt with that question, which was did the FRY leadership maintain support for the Contact Group plan, which is different from the question now just asked, which is what did Slobodan Milosevic express in relation to its support for the Bosnian Serbs. So there are two different questions contain in the same paragraph. They may -- we may reach the same result, but I'm not sure that that's what my colleague is driving at.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Treanor answered the first question at page 84, line 6, at least on my computer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Page 84, line 6 on my computer says, "Judge Moloto: Thank you so much."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm two lines away from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm looking at page 84, line 15, going 14 November 1994, you said that the FRY leadership did maintain support for contract group plan. If I could have 65 ter. I thought that's what we were dealing with, and perhaps I misunderstood what this exhibit was for, the purpose of this exhibit was for. I thought this was going to be documentation, in fact, that the FRY leadership did support the FRY leadership plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's exactly what it's for. The question was was there support. Mr. Treanor said yes. I then asked him what did Slobodan Milosevic say in this session in relation to support for the Bosnian Serbs in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think we're thinking cross-purposes, but that's -- well, let's just proceed and see where we get to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, maybe if I might just try to come to the rescue. That question of whether the FRY leadership supported the Contact Group plan was answered up above at page 84, line 8 to 10. Now, here Madam Sutherland is looping that answer before she puts the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this session Slobodan Milosevic indicated -- continued to indicate his support for the plan in that connection. I would draw the Court's attention to the very bottom of the page in the English translation where he says: "The standpoint of the entire world on five superpowers is absolutely categorical. These talks can be continued only if the plan is accepted." "They," meaning the Bosnian Serb leaders, "do not realise how little space we have for our manoeuvres, and this was the best we could get. They resigned themselves to their fate, and said, all right. It is quite clear that the Serbs have the right to confederation with Yugoslavia. I mean, then it is one state." I'm sorry, I think "they" actually means the international community there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I can take you to page 29 of the B/C/S and page 32 of the English translation. Does he talk there about -- about achieving goals?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry on which page of the English?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Page 32 of the English translation and page 29 of the B/C/S. I think it's at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I have it now. Sorry. Yes. Now, this -- the passage that I'd like to call the Court's attention to is the second paragraph at the top of the page. Here the "they" in question is the Bosnian Serb leaders. "It is not the question anymore whether they can accomplish that goal, because we promptly advised them that it was impossible to achieve the goal they wanted to achieve. We also told them that the politics is the art of the possible and not the art of the impossible. It is simply impossible that the international community will get along with the fact that two-thirds of the population, including Croats and Muslims, are crammed into less than half of the territory. Trust me, I did not -- did not expect that they would give us half of the territory." And the "they" in that sentence being the international community.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And again on page 30 of the B/C/S and 33 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here again Slobodan Milosevic refers to what the international community had agreed to. And says at the top of the page: "And all that happens after so much suffering. We endured everything. We went through all the sanctions, and we came to the point when the entire international community says, "All right. You are not the aggressors. Half of Bosnia and Herzegovina is yours, and you have the right to merge with Serbia and Montenegro. They say," they being the Bosnian Serb leaders, "No, and we will take even more by force. We will prolong the war. That is what I call complete madness."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, can those pages be admitted, that is pages --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's right. They are so admitted. They may please be given an exhibit number. And they are admitted with their corresponding B/C/S pages.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That will be Exhibit P226, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So at this time, being November 1994, did the Bosnian Serb leadership still say that they wanted 70 -- at least 70 per cent of the territory?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 02344 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They continued to refuse to accept the Contact Group plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: At this session, which is the 46th session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly, held on the 11th of November, 1994, and which continued on the 23rd of November, 1994, did Momcilo Krajisnik discuss the Contact Group maps and how they related to the strategic goals?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He made reference to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could take you to page 164 and 165 of the English translation and page 146 of the B/C/S. Can you tell the Court what Momcilo Krajisnik said at this session?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm -- I'm sorry, I'm having trouble identifying the passage. All the pages seem to be numbered 350 on the copy I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's also true of the English translation we have. It's -- if I can take you to where it says page 35 in the English translation, which is halfway down the page on page 164 of e-court, where Chairman Krajisnik starts the discussion. And it's down towards the bottom of that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I could be of some assistance, I have the two specific pages I could -- if the usher could give them to the witness, that might be of some help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sutherland --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There seems to be more than one page 35 in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You may want to check with Ms. Sutherland to make sure I have the same document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yeah. That's what's on the screen now. Mr. Treanor, if you can look -- don't worry about the pages. They can come up on e-court. Usher, could you return those documents to the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor if you look at the bottom of the -- what's on the screen now in the English translation. Six lines up from the -- seven lines up. "I would like to ask you not to discuss the maps at all." And then on the second to last line of that page. "If you want to ask me, I will tell you the Serbian land..." and it continues. And then it continues over the page on page 165 of e-court, of the English translation. What is Mr. Krajisnik saying there in relation to the maps and how they relate to the strategic goals?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
