utterances.text: Well, he notes here: "I have an accurate conclusion that we have the strategic goals. We know exactly where the boundary lines run. It is the Una River, the Sava River, the Drina River, the Neretva River, the sea, et cetera."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So what's the Bosnian Serb leadership's concern at this point?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they're still concerned to achieve those goals.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may page 100 -- page 1 and 164 and 165 be admitted into evidence and page 1 and 146 of the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do so, could I just be on the same page with you, Mr. Treanor. You've just read where they say: "I have an accurate conclusion. We have the strategic goals. We know exact which are the boundary lines are," and then he mentions those lines, and then the question was: What did the Serb leadership -- Bosnian Serb leadership want? And you said those goals, but those goals, you say they have already.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they've adopted those goals as goals. A goal is something to be achieved. They hadn't been achieved in their entirety yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess that is the question. What was outstanding? What was not achieved at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, along the Sava River the Bosnian Serbs did not control the whole southern bank of the river. So the corridor was not as satisfactory as they would have wanted in that -- in that area. And the Drina, there were still places in the Drina valley that they did not control. They did not have -- occupy much -- perhaps no territory on the eastern bank of the Neretva River, and they had not achieved an outlet to the sea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. And those pages are then admitted into evidence. May they please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P227, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, by the end of 1994, did the Bosnian Serb leadership still want to unite with the FRY or the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 06680 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And how was this conveyed to the FRY leadership?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at this -- at this time, this time being November 1994, an interview with Momcilo Krajisnik was published in a Bosnian Serb newspaper containing his views on the situation on that matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have page 9 of the English translation and page 4 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What did Mr. Krajisnik say in this article in relation to wanting to unite with Serbia or the FRY?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for instance, at the bottom of the page in the English, in the line beginning with "State," he says: "We feel that our goal is not a confederation. We want to be united with the Republic of Serbia into a single state because a confederation is not a state. If their proposal is such, then we can choose another version and demand that we be independent and that we unite as such. I'm not the least bit afraid of whether Serbia will want this. Serbia is not an individual. Serbia is the people whose hearts go out to us and who understand us."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Does he also mention -- make mention to Sarajevo in this article?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And without reading it into the record, what does he -- what does he say?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he says that Serb -- Sarajevo will be the capital of the Serbs in Bosnia, but one day Belgrade will be the capital of all the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may that document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is so admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P228, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, can you tell the Chamber very briefly what was happening between December 1994 and August 1995. Very briefly, please?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very briefly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We have five minutes before the end of today's session.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bosnia a cease-fire was, in fact, reached at the end of 1994, which was scheduled to last for four months. All three parties signed that. In Croatia progress was made in negotiations between the government of Croatia and the Republic of Serbian Krajina. An economic agreement was signed in December 1994. However, things didn't continue to go so well in Croatia in January. President Tudjman announced that he would refuse the extension of the mandate of UNPROFOR in Croatia after the end of March 1995, and the republic of -- the RSK renounced the economic agreement and at one point closed the highway through Western Slavonia that had been opened pursuant to that agreement. At the end of April the cease-fire in BH expired, attempts to have it extended having failed, and the next day the 1st of May, 1995, Croatian forces invaded western Slavonia in Croatia and, in fact, occupied that entire territory. After that, military operations resumed in Bosnia. For instance, in the next few months the safe haven of Srebrenica and Zepa were taken by Bosnian Serb forces, and Croatian forces took the city of -- the town of Grahovo in Bosnia at -- toward the end of July 1995, and a few days later they launch Operation Storm against the RSK and within a few days had eliminated all of its territory except for the area of Eastern Slavonia. So that was the situation as of the beginning of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And we have Srebrenica in Bosnia at the end -- beginning of July, middle of July?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in July, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know we're five minutes before finishing, but I'm about to move on to another rather extended exhibit. If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would you like to break at this point?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Then that brings us to the end of the day's session. Adjourned to tomorrow at 9.00, same courtroom. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 11th day of November, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24
